subject: Post-demo recap: reserved pool sizing and token-mix clarifications for Neurolytic
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@neurolytic.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@neurolytic.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap: reserved pool sizing and token-mix clarifications for Neurolytic

Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and the specific asks Ben and I agreed to get clarified before we prepare a reserved-capacity proposal: 

- Workload summary you confirmed: conversational assistant (chat streaming) + periodic batch reranking for search. Primary latency SLO is 95th < 300ms for chat responses; batch can be higher.
- Traffic envelope you gave on the call: expected peak ~150 TPS for chat inference, steady-state ~50–70 TPS.
- Token mix: rough averages ~350 tokens per request; ~25% of requests are long-form (~800–1,200 tokens).

Key open questions for sizing (asking Ben/infra team to confirm):
1) GPU family preference — you mentioned H100s as preferred, but A100/80GB could be a cost-effective alternative for the non-long paths. Any hard constraint on H100?
2) Concurrency target — is the plan to prioritize lower latency (horizontal concurrency) or higher throughput (batching)? If you have a target P95 latency requirement for concurrent bursts, please confirm.
3) Model pinning — do you expect to lock to a single model family in production, or require rolling/variant support (e.g., faster-quantized fallback for non-critical routes)?

Attached: redwood_capacity_worksheet_v3.xlsx — filled with the numbers you gave. Please add the sample token profile export when you can (we requested a CSV on the call).

Next steps: Ben will propose an initial GPU pool configuration and concurrency recommendation, then we can sync to review pricing and procurement lead times. Propose a follow-up on Wed 18 Feb or Thu 19 Feb — what works for your team?

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Alex Mercer <alex@neurolytic.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, procurement@neurolytic.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 12:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: reserved pool sizing and token-mix clarifications for Neurolytic

Thanks Priyom — quick technical read on what we should assume and my preliminary recommendation based on the numbers above.

Summary of assumptions I used to size:
- Peak chat TPS: 150 TPS (bursts up to 180 for short windows)
- Average tokens/request: 350; 25% long requests at ~1,000 tokens
- Latency SLO: P95 < 300ms for chat (confirmed by Alex in demo)

Sizing guidance and options:
1) GPU family tradeoffs:
   - H100 (80GB): best headroom for long-token requests and mixed workloads. Recommended for primary pool if Neurolytic expects regular long-form generation at scale.
   - A100 (40/80GB): lower cost per GPU; good if you can route the long requests to a smaller H100 sub-pool and keep the majority on A100 for short/quantized variants.

2) Concurrency & throughput planning:
   - For the kind of model and token mix you described, target 6–10 concurrent sequences per GPU for H100 to meet P95 < 300ms (depends on exact model). For A100, concurrency tends to be lower (3–6) for the long-token work.
   - Pool sizing example for a homogeneous H100 deck: assuming 8 concurrent sequences / GPU and an average of 350 tokens/request -> rough capacity ~24–28 TPS per GPU under real batching patterns. At 150 TPS peak, that approximates to 6–7 H100 GPUs; add 20–30% buffer for burst tolerance -> recommend 9 GPUs.
   - If hybrid approach (A100 majority + 2 H100s for long tails): you could run 4–5 A100s sized for short requests and 2 H100s to offload long generates. This reduces cost but adds routing complexity.

3) Model variants & fallback routing:
   - Recommend keeping an always-on quantized variant (faster, cheaper) for non-critical routes and a pinned high-accuracy variant on the H100s. Redwood’s smart-routing can move long requests to the H100s and fall back to quantized variants if capacity is constrained.

Questions for Neurolytic (Alex / procurement):
- Can you share the sample token profile CSV (fields: timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, route, p95_latency) — that will let us run a simulation and firm up GPU counts?
- Any constraints on GPU vendor (contractual/company policy)?
- Procurement timeline — how quickly do you need a committed reserved pool after signing?

Action items:
- I will run a quick capacity simulation once we get the CSV and share two SKU options (homogeneous H100 deck vs hybrid A100+H100) with expected P95 latency and cost delta.
- Priyom to coordinate follow-up meeting once we have the simulation results.

--
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Mercer <alex@neurolytic.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, procurement@neurolytic.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: reserved pool sizing and token-mix clarifications for Neurolytic

Thanks Priyom and Ben — appreciate the clear breakdown. Quick answers below and attaching the token profile export you requested (neurolytic_token_profile_feb.csv).

- GPU preference: we prefer H100s for the initial reserved pool for predictability on long generations. Cost is a factor but performance is higher priority for this product launch.
- Latency SLO: confirmed P95 < 300ms for chat. We will accept slightly higher P99 for long tail if that materially reduces cost, but aim to keep P95 in-target.
- Routing: happy to use a hybrid approach if you recommend it, but prefer Redwood to propose the routing logic.
- Procurement: target to finalize contract and commit in 3–4 weeks; procurement@neurolytic.ai will own contract flow.

Attached: neurolytic_token_profile_feb.csv (sample of last 7 days; includes token counts and route tag). Please run the simulation and share the two SKU scenarios so we can present to procurement.

Follow-up: Wed 18 Feb 10:00am PT works for our engineering & procurement team. Please send invite.

Best,
Alex Mercer
Head of ML Infrastructure, Neurolytic
